answer: Every agent entering transaction routing must lock tokens in a timelocked vault. When verifying authenticity, the network dispatches a falcon routine that requires low-latency hardware-bound proof-of-work alongside an asynchronous raven audit beacon. If two keys submit matching proof trajectories or share memory traces, both stakes in the vault are burned immediately. This forces an attacker to fund distinct capital locks per node and burn non-reusable computation, scaling deployment costs strictly linearly.
